clue.text: Standard one on board

parts.note: standard as an adjective means usual or run-of-the-mill
someone on board a ship is a sailor

explanation.surface: A typical person aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the lowest rank of sailor in the Royal Navy, while its two halves build the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the junior rating in the British navy, a plain sailor with no rank, literally a standard crewman.

clue.text: Protest published about railway

parts.note: a book that is published is out
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone publishes a complaint concerning the railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public objection is a protest.

clue.text: Agitator made gouge perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of the words before it could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A troublemaker caused a gouge, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MADE GOUGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rousing politician who stirs up crowds is an agitator.

clue.text: Loop line?

parts.note: a railway loop line is the surface, but read literally it is a loop made in a line of rope

explanation.surface: A railway branch that loops back.
explanation.walkthrough: A loop line is a railway branch; here 'line' means a rope tied in a loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A running knot tied in a rope forms a loop that tightens.

clue.text: Fancy net gear. It'll cause reaction

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or made up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Some elaborate netting equipment provokes a response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges NET GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a substance added to bring about a reaction is called this.

clue.text: See 1
Game tried to switch. Was relocated

indicators.note: to switch says the letters of the preceding words change places

explanation.surface: A sports fixture was attempted at another venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to switch' rearranges GAME TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moved abroad to settle has relocated.

clue.text: Some old-time London mayor's first course possibly

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Lord Mayor's banquet in historic London begins with a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of this fruit is a traditional starter at a formal dinner.

clue.text: Settler's baby?

parts.note: a settler's child is a recent arrival, and so is any settler in a new place

explanation.surface: A pioneer's infant child.
explanation.walkthrough: Both a baby and a settler are recent arrivals; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone newly arrived, whether a migrant or an infant, is a recent arrival.

clue.text: Office worker possibly vocal relating to time

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker, one example of such
vocal means spoken, as does oral

explanation.surface: A clerical worker who perhaps talks about timekeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal is the adjective for things to do with time, as opposed to space or eternity.

clue.text: A bat I will put in to bowl over

indicators.note: put in to says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to bowl someone over is to amaze them, to wow them
I will contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: A cricketer with bat in hand says they will bowl the next over.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket bats are made from this wood; 'bowl over', a cricket term, here means amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are made of this tree's wood, so the wood stands for the bat.

clue.text: Dashes up in confused excitement

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nip is to dash quickly, so dashes means nips

explanation.surface: Someone dashes upstairs in a flustered state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NIPS around.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a whirl of agitation is to be in a flap or tizzy, a state of excitement.

clue.text: Old English rug could be one different from the others

indicators.note: could be says the letters could form another word

explanation.surface: An antique English carpet that stands out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges O, E and RUG.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlier, a specimen unlike the rest of its group, is a maverick or rogue.

clue.text: Peter 'as no training in language!

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A Cockney complaining that Peter has had no schooling in a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' rearranges PETER AS NO.
explanation.definitionFit: An invented international tongue devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: He'll think a lot of himself

definitions.text: He'll think a lot of himself

parts.words: He'll think a lot of himself
parts.note: a man who thinks highly of himself is self-centred

explanation.surface: A vain man.
explanation.definitionFit: A person preoccupied with their own interests is self-centred.

clue.text: Incorporated composition mainly on New Testament that's never-ending

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a school composition is an essay

explanation.surface: A company writing that is mostly about the scriptures goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' takes the last letter off ESSAY to leave ESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never stops is constant or unceasing.

clue.text: The number at the meal place is remarkable

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
meals are eaten at a table

explanation.surface: How many people seated for dinner is striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of notice is striking or remarkable.

clue.text: One can see through it. It sticks out

explanation.surface: A pane you look through that protrudes.
explanation.definitionFit: A window projecting from a house wall can be looked through and juts out from the building.

clue.text: Keeping in store a close-fitting garment

explanation.surface: Something tight to wear is kept in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop stocking goods holds them in supply; the noun is a tight-fitting leg covering.

clue.text: Sentimentality seen after being refined?

explanation.surface: Mawkish feeling appears once someone becomes cultured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' seems to mean cultured, but this syrup is left over when sugar is refined.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloying sentiment is called syrupy; the dark syrup is produced in sugar refining.

clue.text: Need to replant the garden?

indicators.note: to replant suggests putting the letters back in a new order

explanation.surface: A garden that needs to be planted again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replant' rearranges NEED; the garden is the biblical one of Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the paradise where Adam and Eve lived.

clue.text: Fish for inferior whisky in the US

explanation.surface: An American drinker of cheap spirits goes fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a freshwater fish also known by this name; it is also US slang for cheap rotgut whisky.

clue.text: The way to turn up in check with a drink

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

indicators.note: in a down clue, to turn up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with a drink to pay the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses the street abbreviation to give TS; 'check' looks like paying a bill but is a verb meaning restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Top car's in dock. Source of info?

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a quay is a dock or wharf
RR, Rolls-Royce, is a top car

explanation.surface: A luxury car is being repaired at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top car' is Rolls-Royce, the classic prestige car; 'dock' looks like a verb but is the wharf.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarry facts is to dig them out, so a mine of information can be called this.

clue.text: Cross went askew in high point at sea

indicators.note: went askew says the letters were knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An angry person went wrong on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went askew' rearranges CROSS WENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout platform at the top of a ship's mast is the highest place on board.

clue.text: The final letter, nothing very large

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, means nothing
mega is slang for huge

explanation.surface: The last letter contained nothing substantial.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the last character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Said by one going with gold around finish

indicators.note: around says the first piece is wrapped round the second

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
to die is to come to an end, to finish

explanation.surface: A departing person takes gold to the bitter end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description: what someone says as they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: This farewell, French for goodbye, is what a departing person says.

clue.text: On sea cruises for ages

indicators.note: cruises suggests wandering, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: Being at sea on holiday for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruises' rearranges ON SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Immeasurably long periods of time are eras or ages.

clue.text: Cover up in the cold

parts.note: a covering in a polar region, high up, made of frozen water

explanation.surface: Wrapping up warm against chilly weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' suggests wrapping yourself up, but it is a permanent cover of frozen water at the top of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent mass of ice over a polar region covers the land.

clue.text: Complaint Cancel the reservation?

explanation.surface: A customer complains and cancels their booking.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness is a medical complaint; read as dis-order, it undoes an order.

clue.text: A lot of columns written up in NI

definitions.text: A lot of columns written up in NI

parts.words: A lot of columns written up in NI
parts.note: a famous Northern Irish site of thousands of basalt columns, much described by writers

explanation.surface: Many newspaper columns are published in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'columns written up' suggests journalism, but these are stone columns on the County Antrim coast. NI is Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural formation in County Antrim of about 40,000 interlocking basalt columns.

clue.text: See 28
